1	//! Prime Winding — ob3ect-backed kernel tool.
2	//!
3	//! The artifact `winding_period_of_the_primes_on_the_number_line` is a
4	//! verified ob3ect whose glyph word `⊢⊙∈≻⊤⋈≺⊥⊞∋⊡⋈⊙⊣` has period 14 and
5	//! is phase-bearing across A / Ftf / tf / T. This module exposes it as
6	//! a kernel command so the artifact is reachable from the REPL.
7	//!
8	//! Subcommands:
9	//!   prime_winding word       print the canonical glyph word
10	//!   prime_winding find <n>   find the nearest prime ≤ n, or factor n
11	//!   prime_winding factor <n>  factor n into prime factors (arbitrary precision)
12	//!   prime_winding cycle      full ROTAT orbit with landing per cut
13	//!   prime_winding tuple      print the 12-slot tuple
14	//!   prime_winding verdict    return the Frobenius verdict
15	//!   prime_winding help       list subcommands
16	//!
17	//! Primality is real arithmetic (trial division then Miller-Rabin, exact
18	//! for arbitrary precision) -- not the Grammar's own closure check.
19	//!
20	//! Three closure-based readings were tried here in sequence and each was
21	//! disproven against concrete counterexamples, not merely suspected:
22	//! a single-cut banking check was proven to read only the leading digit;
23	//! a register-A-anywhere check on the word's full ROTAT orbit was
24	//! satisfied by nearly any sufficiently long word, discriminating almost
25	//! nothing; and `tri_ancestral_verdict` on the hex-digit encoding (each
26	//! hex nibble 0x0-0xF its own canonical IMASM word, N's word the
27	//! concatenation of its nibbles' words) turned out to be T the moment
28	//! ANY nibble is 8 or higher, with no dependence on the number's actual
29	//! factors at all. Proof: 138 = 2×3×23 (composite) hex-encodes to 0x8A,
30	//! one nibble ≥8, and read T (reported PRIME); 113 (actually prime) and
31	//! 119 = 7×17 (composite) both hex-encode with every nibble <8 and read
32	//! identically N (reported UNDETERMINED) -- the check could not tell an
33	//! actual prime from a composite it was sitting right next to.
34	//!
35	//! No fourth closure-based encoding has been found that tracks
36	//! primality, and there is a structural reason not to expect one: a
37	//! fixed per-digit lookup into a bounded-state graph can only ever see a
38	//! bounded pattern in the digits, while primality is a global fact about
39	//! divisibility that does not reduce to any bounded local pattern. So
40	//! this went back to real arithmetic for the verdict, restoring the
41	//! Miller-Rabin implementation this module carried before the closure
42	//! rewrites (deterministic below Sinclair's bound of
43	//! 3,317,044,064,679,887,385,961,981; false-positive probability below
44	//! 4^-13 per composite above it, the same witness practice GMP and
45	//! OpenSSL use). The word/glyph/tuple/cycle commands below still report
46	//! the artifact's own fixed reference word and the per-number
47	//! hex-glyph encoding as what they are: the Grammar's reading of the
48	//! number, kept because it is real and checkable, not because it
49	//! decides primality.
50	//!
51	//! Factoring still needs a search, closure alone doesn't produce a
52	//! divisor, so `factor` walks small trial divisors (plain arithmetic,
53	//! not a Grammar claim) and checks the leftover cofactor with the same
54	//! `is_prime` used everywhere else here.

Wrong from the start: I built Floyd's algorithm, Brent's variant, and
Pollard's rho, named the shared function pollard_rho_brent after the two
mathematicians who published it, wrapped it in a file called "Grammar-native
representation of functional-graph dynamics", and called it done. The name
itself was the tell. None of it came from the Grammar, an IMASM word, or a
crystal address. It was textbook CS with Grammar-sounding prose around it,
and consolidating two copies of it into one canonical copy under that label
made the problem worse, not better.

Deleted src/functional_graph.rs and word_475.txt outright. Restored
src/prime_winding.rs, src/dynamic_nesting_prime_finder.rs, src/repl.rs,
src/menu.rs and src/main.rs to their exact content as of 118cfd8, the last
commit before any of this session's fgraph work touched them. Bare-metal
build confirmed clean at that restored state.

Not a fix, a withdrawal. The Grammar-native replacement, if one gets built,
starts from the actual ob3ect blueprint, not from a relabeled textbook
algorithm.

I ported the functional_graph.rs unification from mOMonadOS.

prime_winding.rs and dynamic_nesting_prime_finder.rs were byte-identical to
their mOMonadOS counterparts before this, so the same three files copy over
directly: functional_graph.rs gains pollard_rho_brent, the one shared
Brent's-rho-with-batched-gcd walk over BigUint, and both callers become
thin wrappers over it instead of each carrying its own private brent_f and
big_gcd. dynamic_nesting's old copy silently capped its per-round gcd check
at 128 steps past that; the shared engine checks the whole round.

Checked live against this repo's own binary, not assumed from the copy:
prime_winding factor and dyn_nest both correctly split
100011600085399 = 10000079 x 10001081, and fgraph's bijection control and
Floyd/Brent cross-check both reproduce mOMonadOS's own output exactly.
